title.narrative: Insight Crime Latin America - Core Support

description.narrative:
InSight Crime is a non-governmental organization with 13 years of experience that has become the major reference for the coverage and analysis of organized crime and citizen security in Latin America and the Caribbean.
Insight Crime is a regional actor that promotes the debate on organized crime, it is founded within the region and its activities tackle cross¬border challenges that are common to almost all region’s countries. They contribute to deepen and inform the debate about organized crime in the Americas by providing regular reporting, analysis, investigation, and policy suggestions on how to tackle the multiple challenges it presents, and promotes increased transparency and reduced corruption in the region. In this sense, their work contribute to goal of increasing regional cooperation and dialogue in the areas of human rights and the rule of law, strengthening regional solutions, and strengthening citizens’ capacity to influence policy decisions. Sida assessment is that the contribution is well aligned with the regional strategy for Latin America and that a core support can be beneficial to strengthen this partner´s work and their influence in LAC.
This contribution concerns support to InSight Crime in the form of of core funding, which will be used to strengthen the overall activities of InSight Crime during the next three years (2024-2026).

InSight Crime är en icke-statlig organisation med 13 års erfarenhet som har blivit den viktigaste referensen för bevakning och analys av organiserad brottslighet och medborgarnas säkerhet i Latinamerika och Karibien. Insight Crime är en regional aktör som bidrar till debatten om organiserad brottslighet. Organisationen grundades och har sin bas i regionen. Dess verksamhet hanterar gränsöverskridande utmaningar som är gemensamma för nästan alla regionens länder. De bidrar till att fördjupa och informera debatten om organiserad brottslighet i Amerika genom att tillhandahålla regelbunden journalistisk rapportering, analys, utredning och policyförslag om hur man hanterar de många utmaningar som den organiserade brottsligheten utgör, och främjar ökad öppenhet och minskad korruption i regionen. På så sätt bidrar deras arbete till målet att öka regionalt samarbete och dialog inom områdena mänskliga rättigheter och rättsstatsprincipen, stärka regionala lösningar och stärka medborgarnas kapacitet att påverka politiska beslut. Sida bedömer att bidraget ligger väl i linje med den regionala strategin för Latinamerika och att ett kärnstöd kan vara att föredra för att stärka denna partners arbete och deras inflytande i LAC.
Detta bidrag avser stöd till InSight Crime i form av kärnfinansiering, som kommer att användas för att stärka den övergripande verksamheten för InSight Crime under de kommande tre åren (2024-2026).

InSight Crime will receive core support from sida for the next three years (2024-2025-2026). The main goal of the intervention is to strengthen the partner´s overall objective of deepening, informing, and provoking "debate about organized crime and citizen security in the Americas by providing regular reporting, analysis, and investigation, as well as policy suggestions on how to tackle the multiple challenges they present".
According to InSight Crime´s strategic document for 2023-2025, the specific objectives for the period are the following:
1. Strengthen the regional outlook of the partners work in their efforts on understanding and explaining criminal dynamics throughout the Americas.
2. Support the social media and communications objective particularly including podcast as a new communication format.
3. Reinforce the retention and training of staff plan to support their internal capacity-building.
4. Support the investigative priorities planned for the period, in particular those related to environmental crime, threats to democracy and rule of law, and the understanding of organized crime and gender.

title.narrative: Grant Agreement InSight Crime - Sida Regional Latin America
Decision on Contribution 16560 - InSight Crime Core Support

description.narrative:
In 2025 InSight Crime worked towards improving the integration between the different teams that make up the core operations of the organization.
Main achievements:
• InSight Crime investigations have revealed malfeasance and corruption, and analyzed failures in systems of accountability in the private and public sectors, while exposing corrupt and criminal actors. This work has generated the public awareness that drives pressure on the relevant actors to take appropriate action to hold individuals and institutions to account and make systemic changes. Their investigations in some cases were used as inputs for security and justice institutions and in judicial proceedings contributing to more informed public debate and reinforcing demands for accountability.
• Their work has strengthened and supported regional cooperation. Their investigations, datasets, and analytical frameworks have equipped NGOs, journalists, academics, and advocacy groups to monitor and understand organized crime, document abuses, and engage with institutional actors, while their alliance building and participation in cooperative civil society activities has contributed to stronger regional networks by facilitating cross-border collaboration with other media outlets, NGOs, and academic institutions.
• They have produced multiple investigations and analysis pieces tackling the issues of gender-based violence linked to organized crime, environmental crime, and the criminal exploitation of migration flows (all areas related to Sida's regional development cooperation strategy). This work has supported more informed, rights-based approaches to these issues.
• InSight crime has focused activities on their strategic growth and organizational development, so they have consolidated internal coordination and have improved the impact process review. The team created a new institutional impact framework, which offers a conceptual model for InSight Crimes impact and outlines their guiding impact goals and pathways to achieving them.
• During 2025, the Multimedia and Communications (MAC) and Flagship (website editorial) teams focused on integration of the website with the social media platforms, both in terms of the internal processes and the publications. As a result, the social media strategy increasingly focused on engagement and interaction within each platform, prioritizing audience connection and brand positioning over direct traffic to the site. MAC strengthened InSight Crimes digital presence and adapted to changing content consumption habits.
• In response to the rapid and profound changes to the fundraising environment, the partner strengthened the fundraising unit created in the previous cycle. This included integrating a team of researchers, editors, and administrators who mapped the funding ecosystem, monitored new funding opportunities, and presented more than a dozen proposals. As part of this process, they are exploring new areas of private sector engagement, in line with their objectives to help better inform the private sector to reduce the vulnerability of economic actors to being threatened, coopted, or exploited by organized crime. Moreover, they are consolidating and strengthen individual donations campaign and have structured monetization by organizing exclusive donor events.
• The Monitoring and Data Analysis (MAD) team took the lead role in one of the central objectives for institutional strengthening: seeking to integrate artificial intelligence into distinct processes within the organization. This involved a three-step process: identifying workflows within the organization, determining AI integration opportunities based on a diagnosis of those workflows, and generating testing spaces for AI tools.
• Over the year, the team refined its understanding of what performs best on each social media platform, achieving strong engagement levels and maintaining a diverse weekly content grid. On average, 900 posts were published per month across platforms. The partner has explained that 2025 marked a decisive shift from using social media primarily as a bridge to the website toward positioning each platform as a strategic space for engagement, dissemination of information and analysis, brand positioning, and product development in its own right. In the report, they present the specific achievements in each platform: LinkedIn, Youtube, Instagram, X and Facebook.
• The partner continues creating strategic alliances with other media partners, academic institutions and other key actors. Moreover, InSight Crime directors and senior staff participated in numerous conferences, forums, and other public events, as well as private briefings and closed-door events with policymakers, security forces, and other regional and international decision makers. Through this work, they helped meet their goals of contributing to more informed policymaking and security strategies, more informed, higher quality work by civil society organizations, and stronger civil society networks.
• The partner organized eight virtual panels and one in-person event. According to InSight Crime, these events served as an alternative mechanism for disseminating the findings to better inform the public, civil society, policymakers, and security forces, while also acting as an important tool for engagement and civil society network building.
• In 2025 their work were cited a record-number of times, with over 5,000 media mentions which maintains the position of InSight Crime as a key source of information on organized crime in Latin America and the Caribbean, underlining the importance of engagement with other media as a way of shaping debate and informing the public.
• InSight Crime has prioritized the capacity building programs inside the organization. 18 people from 11 countries participated in InSight Crimes internship program in 2025, providing operational support for the organization while helping train and educate participants in valuable skills so they can contribute to this field in the future. Moreover, they carried out nine internal trainings, which were given to 34 staff members in a diverse range of critical skills and key knowledge for the field such as navigating hostile environments, interview techniques, data visualization, media monitoring, and the use of AI.
